newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen opening mixed after data, HP slips.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen opening mixed after data, HP slips.

text.p: Wall Street markets were seen opening mixed on Friday after housing starts data and losses in Dow component Hewlett-Packard Co offset momentum from Thursday's gains.
"We are probably going to give some ground because of Hewlett-Packard, and then superimposed on that you have housing starts," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential.
"We are talking small gradations but you are probably going to get a mixed opening."
Hewlett-Packard fell sharply in pre-market activity, trading at 53-3/4, down from its close of 58-7/8.
U.S. April housing starts data came in up 2.6 percent to a 1.473 million unit annual rate, higher than the forecast of 1.43 million.
Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co, said the data "are likely to be a negative for the market.
"It's so tough to call how the market will open today. Right now we are likely to have a show-me opening."
The long bond was down 9/32 with a yield rising to 6.89 percent from Thursday's close at 6.87 percent.
